title: Improving Heterogeneous Graph Contrastive Learning Robustness via Hierarchical Vulnerability Protection

problem.claim: Heterogeneous Graph Contrastive Learning is vulnerable to perturbation attacks because heterogeneous graph structures are inherently fragile.

gap.claim: Existing heterogeneous-graph defenses primarily address supervised scenarios and protect all nodes equally through structural pruning, which can remove sufficient structural information needed for self-supervised HGCL.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes HVP-HGCL, which identifies vulnerable nodes and protects them across aggregation layers to improve HGCL robustness.
The Vulnerability Detection module determines which nodes are more sensitive to attacks in self-supervised scenarios.
The Hierarchical Protection module safeguards vulnerable nodes from attack noise across different aggregation layers.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe HVP-HGCL as a novel approach to heterogeneous graph contrastive learning with hierarchical vulnerability protection.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that HVP-HGCL improves robustness against adversarial attacks.
The authors report that HVP-HGCL achieves competitive performance on downstream tasks.
The authors report that HVP-HGCL preserves sufficient structural information for effective contrastive learning.

narrative_sequence.summary: HGCL represents heterogeneous graphs without detailed annotations.
HGCL is vulnerable to perturbation attacks, while existing defenses focus mainly on supervised settings and may remove useful structure in self-supervised settings.
The authors argue that node vulnerability differs across nodes and that attack influence accumulates across aggregation layers.
HVP-HGCL detects vulnerable nodes and protects them hierarchically across aggregation layers.
The method is reported to improve robustness while retaining structural information and achieving competitive downstream-task performance.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the perturbation attack models or threat assumptions.
The abstract does not identify datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not explain the vulnerability-detection criterion or hierarchical-protection mechanism in detail.
The abstract does not provide ablations, computational costs, or failure cases.
